books.title: Know Yourself Kindly
books.sub: Where your lens came from, who you are now, and who you are becoming
books.line: Start with yourself: your history, your wiring, your feelings, your worth and how your mind works.
books.blurb: Before you can share a life well, it helps to know your own. This short book starts with you. Where did your way of seeing things come from: the home you grew up in, the old rules, the things life taught you? How are you wired today: your energy, your weather, the words that land and the ones that sting? And who are you becoming, one small step at a time? Along the way it explains how feelings work, why your worth is not a score, why personality is more like a set of dials than a box, and how minds work differently, from ADHD and autism to sensory and learning differences, with ways to meet in the middle. Every chapter has everyday scenes, words you could use and one small thing to try this week. Nothing here is a test. Read it on your own, at your own pace.

books.title: Heal and Steady
books.sub: Stress, anger, worry, loss and repair, and finding your footing again
books.line: For the heavy days: stress, anger, worry and low mood, grief, repair, change and what matters to you.
books.blurb: Some days are heavy. Stress piles up, anger flares, worry keeps you awake, or a loss changes everything. This book is about steadying yourself through all of it, gently and without blame. It explains what stress does to the body and why it adds up, what anger is for and what helps in the hot minutes, how worry, low mood and trauma work, and when and where to get help. It walks with you through grief in its many forms, through repair and apologies that land, and through the slow work of change, one small step at a time. It ends with what matters to you, and what a good life can mean. Each chapter has words you could use and one small thing to try. Where a chapter touches hard things, it says where to find help. Go at your own pace.

books.title: Understanding Each Other
books.sub: How we hear, see and belong to each other, at home and in every group
books.line: Pace and tone, how words land, how we see each other, belonging, love, groups and helping well.
books.blurb: Two people can care about each other and still fall out of tune. One wants to talk now; the other needs an hour. A comment meant lightly lands hard. This book is about understanding the people around you: at home, in families, with friends, at work and in every group you belong to. It explains how pace and tone pull people apart, how communication really works, and why two people can see the same moment so differently. It looks at why we need to belong, how trust grows and is rebuilt, how love takes many forms, and the quiet pull of the groups we are part of. It ends with helping others well, with kind limits and without burning out. Each chapter has everyday scenes, words you could use and one small thing to try. No blame and no verdicts: just a clearer view and a kinder next step.

books.title: Share the Load
books.sub: The work nobody sees, and a fair, kind way to share it
books.line: For homes, families and teams: seeing the unseen work, one owner per job, and two kinds of fair.
books.blurb: Every shared home, family or team runs on work that nobody sees: noticing the shoes are too small, booking the appointment, remembering bin day. When that work isn’t counted, someone ends up carrying more than anyone realises, and resentment grows quietly. This book helps you see the whole load, kindly and without keeping score. It shows a simple way to check whether the way you share the work can last, how much of a reaction is leftover stress, how to agree what fair means to each of you, and a gentle monthly look-back that catches what weekly chats miss. Each chapter points to a workpaper that puts it to use, free to print from the website. It ends with an afterword that draws the threads of the whole series together. It looks at the setup, never at the person.

workbook.title: The Workpapers: Free Forms, All in One
workbook.sub: Every workpaper from the series, on big pages, to fill in by hand
workbook.line: All the workpapers on large pages, with room to write and spare copies for the weeks ahead.
workbook.blurb: Every workpaper from the Spread Love & Acceptance books, on big pages with room to write. Inside are blank copies of all ten: a quick check of how much you’re carrying, a calm-down kit you make on a calm day, a self-check before you reply to something that stung, a 90-second daily check-in, a one-week log of who did what, a list that gives every job one owner, a monthly look-back, and more. Each one starts with a short page that says when to use it, how long it takes, who fills it in and which book explains it. Then come spare copies for the weeks ahead, a planner for the six-week program and pages for your own notes. The sheets describe what happened, never who someone is. Every form is also free to print or fill in online; this book simply puts them all in one place.
